drivingQuestion: From where is it derived that one must not publicly humiliate another even at the cost of his own life?
outcomeNote: The source is supplied from Tamar's conduct in Genesis 38:25 and nothing is raised against it.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּיזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: נוֹחַ לוֹ לְאָדָם שֶׁיַּפִּיל עַצְמוֹ לְתוֹךְ כִּבְשַׁן הָאֵשׁ וְאַל יַלְבִּין פְּנֵי חֲבֵרוֹ בָּרַבִּים. מְנָלַן? — מִתָּמָר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הִיא מוּצֵאת וְגוֹ׳״.
segments.en: «And Rav Zutra bar Toviya said» that «Rav said; and some say Rav Ḥana bar Bizna said» that «Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said; and some say Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai: It is preferable,» from an ethical perspective, «for one to throw himself into a fiery furnace rather than humiliate another in public. From where do we» derive this? «From Tamar,» the daughter-in-law of Judah, when she was taken out to be burned, «as it is stated: “As she was brought forth,» she sent to her father-in-law, saying I am pregnant by the man to whom these belong, and she said examine these, to whom does this seal, cord and staff belong?” (Genesis 38:25). Despite her dire situation, she did not reveal that she was pregnant with Judah’s child; rather, she left the decision to him, to avoid humiliating him in public.
